_why: Round-3 send-back item 3. `git_policy.pr_state.refs_heads_strip_pattern` is declared `kind: "text"` (always IGNORECASE per CONTRACT's regex-dialect rules) but lib/gitcmd.py used to compile it with a bare re.compile() -- no flags -- so `^refs/heads/` never matched the capitalised `refs/Heads/feat` destination and the branch stayed UNSTRIPPED. pr-state-guard.ps1's own `-replace '^refs/heads/', ''` is case-INSENSITIVE by PowerShell default, so the MASTER already stripped this correctly -- the bug was a Python-port-only divergence (not a parity exception; parity:true), now fixed by routing gitcmd.py through the shared compile_pattern(). 'feat' and the literal unstripped string 'refs/Heads/feat' are given DIFFERENT PR states so the bug (if it recurred) would flip the exit code, not just the branch name in a message: correctly-stripped 'feat' has an OPEN PR (ALLOW); anything else queried against gh finds only a MERGED PR (BLOCK).
